thread.title: Troy Rivetti appointed as U.S. Attorney for Western District of Pennsylvania
thread.title_full: Troy Rivetti appointed as U.S. Attorney for Western District of Pennsylvania

author: Keystone Today
title: Troy Rivetti appointed as U.S. Attorney for Western District of Pennsylvania
text:
Troy Rivetti was appointed as the United States Attorney for the Western District of Pennsylvania, according to a May 27 announcement by the United States District Court for the district. The appointment follows action by the court’s Board of Judges last week, and Rivetti was sworn in by Chief United States District Judge Cathy Bissoon. His appointment becomes effective on May 28 and succeeds a 120-day appointment made in January by the United States Attorney General.
“It is a tremendous honor to be appointed United States Attorney by the judges of the United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania; I am humbled and grateful for the opportunity to continue to serve this office and the citizens and law enforcement partners of our district,” said United States Attorney Rivetti. “The Court’s decision is encouraging, as it assures consistency in the leadership of our office and recognizes the ongoing hard work and outstanding commitment to public service and public safety by our attorneys and staff, both individually and collectively.”
Rivetti has led the office since former U.S. Attorney Eric Olshan resigned in January 2025. He served as Acting U.S. Attorney until November 2025 before returning to his previous role as First Assistant U.S. Attorney until being named U.S. Attorney by then-Attorney General Pamela Bondi in late January 2026.
Rivetti’s career with the Department of Justice spans nearly three decades, including leadership roles such as Acting U.S. Attorney from February to June 2023, First Assistant U.S. Attorney from November 2021 to January 2025, and Chief of Criminal Division from 2019 to 2021 after joining in 1997.
His prosecutorial work has focused on violent crime investigations, large-scale drug trafficking organizations, firearms offenses, and notably co-leading prosecution efforts in United States v. Robert Bowers—the case involving what has been described as “the worst antisemitic mass shooting in U.S. history.” He served as first chair during jury selection, trial proceedings, and sentencing over three months.
Rivetti earned his Bachelor’s degree from Dickinson College before obtaining his Juris Doctor from Georgetown University. He previously worked five years at a Pittsburgh law firm before clerking two years for Judge D. Brooks Smith.
